text:
laura: FYI perf alarm from canary yesterday — p95 jumped ~18% on small-prompt workloads.
jin: saw the alert. which commits were part of that rollout?
marco: release-2026-03-08 included the KV eviction tweak (moved eviction to request path + threshold change) and the batching heuristic rewrite in a separate PR.
sam: did CI flag anything?
perf-ci: perf check for serve-latency-small failed 2/5 runs after merge, but labeled flaky so merge continued.
laura: i did a quick local run — KV cache hit rate fell ~12% in steady state, correlating with higher p95.
jin: starting git bisect between release-2026-03-08 and HEAD now.
marco: note #3432 (kernel-selection reschedule) also landed nearby; watch for interactions.
sam: collect flamegraphs during bisect, use this command:
```
./tools/bisect_perf.sh --bench serve-latency-small --from release-2026-03-08 --to HEAD --collect flame
```
laura: bisect points to two commits together: 8f2b4a7 (batching heuristic changes) and 3c9d2f1 (kv eviction moved inline). individually they look ok, combined they reproduce the regression.
jin: flame shows increased time in schedule_requests and in kv_cache::evict_if_needed on the request hot path.
marco: repro steps attached in thread: small prompts, batch sizes 1-4, cold then warm cache. reproducible on a single A100.
sam: i pushed a revert for the inline eviction (revert 3c9d2f1) to canary. rolling.
ops-bot: Deploy started: canary -> 3 hosts. ID: dpl-2026-177900
laura: canary metrics: p95 back to baseline, kv hit rate recovered. rollback mitigated the issue.
jin: retro takeaway: regression was an emergent interaction between two concurrent changes; CI perf flakiness allowed the bad merge.
marco: action items proposal:
- keep eviction off the request path; design async eviction + backpressure signals
- add a microbenchmark for kv_cache::evict_if_needed to PR checks
- require perf checks to pass 3/3 stable runs for perf-sensitive lanes
- add a lightweight synthetic small-prompt probe in merge gating that runs daily
laura: also add eviction metrics: evict_duration_ms, pre_evict_hits, post_evict_hits, evict_count. instrument logs so regressions are easier to reason about.
sam: CI harness fixes: pin CPU/GPU governor, isolate perf runners, and disable background telemetry during perf runs to reduce noise.
jin: i'll open a PR with microbench + metrics + tightened thresholds. tagging @marco @sam for review.
marco: i'll write a short design doc for async eviction fallback and ensure we add a unit test preventing moving eviction into the request path without a safe fallback.
laura: i'll summarize this for the release postmortem and create a ticket linking to the bisect artifacts. ops-bot, please remind about postmortem ticket.
ops-bot: Reminder: create ticket and link to release postmortem.
laura: nice bisecting everyone, and good catch on the flaky CI. :tada:
